newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Starving N.Korean soldiers take food, money - report.
newsitem.headline: Starving N.Korean soldiers take food, money - report.

text.p: Many soldiers in North Korea's 1.1 million-strong army are starving and roaming famine-hit cities and rural areas with their weapons demanding food and money, Hong Kong's Sunday Morning Post reported.

The newspaper, which based its story on reports from ethnic Korean Chinese returning to China after visits to relatives in the impoverished state, said the accounts contradicted Pyongyang claims that it had been able to keep its army under control.

"In Namyang city, soldiers wandered the streets at night. If they saw a light, they would break into homes threatening people with guns, demanding food and money," Kim Chan-shan, 50, was quoted as saying after returning from a three-week visit.
The soldiers believed only people with relatives in China would be well off enough to afford lighting, Kim said.
Some soldiers also staged night raids to steal animals or force peasants to reveal hidden grain stores, another visitor, Liu Jin-bin, was quoted as saying.
Devastated by floods in 1995 and 1996, North Korea needs at least 1.3 million tonnes of additional food to meet its basic needs this year, a United Nations food aid agency said recently.
North Korean authorities said earlier their food supplies were due to run out by the end of April.
